title: Launchpad shadow rotation + hiring calibration notes (weekly)
body:
Purpose: quick weekly capture from Launchpad shadow rotations and interviewer calibration sessions. This is intentionally raw — notes to synthesize into a Playbook update and a hiring panel checklist next week.

Context summary
- Launchpad is our 30-day ramp program for ICs joining infra/platform teams; we run shadow rotations across eng subteams so new engineers see codebase + oncall basics + interview panels.
- This week we ran three shadow loops (Serving Runtime, Console, Observability) with 5 new joiners + 3 internal rotation buddies. Focus: practical pairing, interview rubric alignment, and early ramp blockers.

Highlights / quick wins
- Serving Runtime rotation: pairing on a small batching perf test. New hire observed kernel selection workflow, submitted 1 small perf PR template (PR linked in artifacts). Buddy Marcos ran a 20-minute walkthrough of the optimizer flags — rated high usefulness by hire.
- Console rotation: showed how rollout flags are configured for canaries. Observed a gap in documentation — the console runbook was missing the rollback checklist for DB migrations. Ellen drafted a rollback checklist in the session (see action items).
- Observability rotation: Diego demoed tracing hooks and how to follow a trace from an API call to the GPU node. New hire suggested a visual cheat-sheet (sequence diagram) — good candidate for a 1-pager.

Interview calibration notes (panel observations)
- Panel mix: 2 Eng interviewers + 1 Hiring manager for loop. We observed mismatch in expected rubric weighting: technical reasoning vs system design vs communication.
- Specific example: Candidate A produced good tradeoffs but the interviewer scored low on "problem decomposition" — divergence appears to stem from unclear rubric labels.
- Recommendation: rephrase rubric labels to concrete behaviors ("decomposes problem into components + data flow" vs current vague "architecture thinking").
- Ask: can we pilot a 1-page rubric cheat sheet for interviewers next week? I can draft and push to PR for review.

Onboarding and team health signals
- New hire sentiment (anonymous pulse): 4/5 for clarity of first-week goals, but 3/5 for access to envs (some credential delays).
- Access friction: two hires lacked access to the internal KMS sandbox for private deployments — blocked for ~36 hours. Cause: ticket routing to security team is inconsistent.
- Buddy program load: buddies reported 6–8 extra hours in the first week; most said they can sustain for 2 people per month but not 4. Suggest: cap pairings and rotate buddies every 2 weeks.

Unresolved questions / risks
- Security routing: who owns triage of KMS sandbox access? Currently ambiguous between eng-platform and security-ops. Jira ENG-2412 opened to resolve ownership (linked).
- Interview capacity: scheduling is backlogged by 18 days for backend ICs — hiring velocity risk for Q3. Could escalate to Talent to add external interviewer pool or shift to async coding tasks.
- New hire loading: potential burnout signal if buddies keep >6 hours of onboarding overhead for multiple hires per quarter. Need a capacity model.

Action items (owners and rough ETA)
- Priya: draft 1-page interviewer rubric cheat sheet and open PR by 2026-07-20.
- Ellen: add rollback checklist to Console runbook and post a short note to #eng-console; ETA 2026-07-16.
- Marcus: follow up with Security-ops to clarify KMS sandbox onboarding flow and update INC/triage doc; link to update in this doc; ETA 2026-07-21.
- Diego & Sofia: create a trace sequence-diagram 1-pager and add to Launchpad repo as `quickstart/trace-cheatsheet.md`; ETA 2026-07-22.
- People Ops (cc Talent): evaluate adding 2 temporary interviewers to reduce scheduling backlog; ask by 2026-07-18.

Suggested changes to Playbook
- Add a short "Troubleshooting access" subsection with step-by-step for KMS, internal VPN, and test data buckets.
- Introduce a buddy-hour cap and optional overlap office hours (one 2-hour slot per week where buddies can answer async questions).
- Convert the interview rubric to behavior-based checkboxes and capture one example answer per level (Good / Ok / Needs work) for consistent scoring.

Anecdotes (useful for qualitative feedback)
- New hire M said: "Seeing a full request trace end-to-end made me feel less intimidated — immediately understood where I could contribute small fixes."
- Buddy L commented: "I loved the rotation format but felt the calendar fragmentation (three 1-hour sessions across different tools) made it hard to retain context. A single 3-hour shadow block might be better."

Next steps for this doc
- Keep as weekly rolling note. I will synthesize into two deliverables: (1) Playbook PR with rollout + access fixes, (2) Interviewer rubric PR. Target ship dates above.

Questions for leadership
- Can we temporarily reassign one experienced buddy from Platform to help with onboarding spikes during mid-July hiring ramp?
- Is there budget/headcount to onboard 1 external interviewer resource to reduce panel wait times?

If you have items to add, drop inline comments here or ping me in #eng-onboarding.
